Monetisation in Kenya: The Real Numbers & the New Rules

7 min read · Updated November 2026 · Free · Written for Kenya
Share: WhatsApp X Facebook Telegram LinkedIn

In Kenya you can start earning from YouTube at 500 subscribers, before any ad money. And from October 2026, Google holds your payouts until you add a KRA PIN.

YouTube has two monetisation levels, and Kenya is on YouTube's official list for the lower one. Most people only know the 1,000-subscriber number, so they skip the first step.

LevelYou needWhat you unlock
Lower tier (fan funding)500 subs + 3 public uploads in 90 days + either 3,000 watch hours (12 months) or 3M Shorts views (90 days)Channel memberships, Super Thanks, Super Chat & Stickers, Shopping
Full YPP1,000 subs + either 4,000 public watch hours (12 months) or 10M Shorts views (90 days)Ad revenue share + YouTube Premium revenue
The Shorts view trap

Since 31 March 2025, the view count on a Short counts every play and replay. YouTube says YPP eligibility and earnings are still based on engaged views, the old, stricter count. Find it in Analytics > Advanced mode. Your "10M" progress is lower than your public counter.

What ad money actually looks like here

Ad rates depend largely on where viewers are and what advertisers pay to reach them. Kenyan YouTuber Thee Pluto has said 1 million views in Kenya pays around KSh 100,000 on average, versus over KSh 1 million for US views. That's one creator's figure, not an official rate, but it's a useful reality check: roughly KSh 100 per 1,000 local views.

5%
Withheld by Google from Kenyan creators' YouTube earnings from September 2026; payouts freeze without a verified KRA PIN in AdSense (Techweez, Business Daily)

The two policies that cost channels their money

  • Inauthentic content (renamed July 2025). Mass-produced or repetitive videos aren't monetisable, including "AI-generated content made with generic or unoriginal templates giving the impression of mass production". Using AI to edit scripts is explicitly fine.
  • Unsatisfying or off-putting content. YouTube's monetisation policy now also lists content that "relies heavily on emotionally manipulative formulas".
  • Reused content. Compilations with little narrative or silent reactions don't qualify. Reactions where you actually comment do.
✗ MYTH

Since May 2026, YouTube punishes AI videos with lower reach.

✓ REALITY

YouTube now detects significant photorealistic AI and adds a label automatically if you didn't. But it says "a disclosure label alone does not change how a video is recommended or whether it's eligible to earn money". What gets channels in trouble is repeatedly failing to disclose, or mass-produced content.

✅ Do this today
⚡ Quick check

Your Shorts show 12 million views in the last 90 days. Have you hit the 10M Shorts threshold for YPP?

Since March 2025 the public counter includes every play and replay. YouTube says eligibility still uses engaged views. Check those in Analytics > Advanced mode.

🧠 Key takeaways
  1. Kenya qualifies for the 500-subscriber fan-funding tier; ad revenue needs 1,000 subs.
  2. Shorts thresholds use engaged views, not the public counter.
  3. Google withholds 5% from Kenyan creators and needs your KRA PIN to pay you.
  4. Mass-produced and emotionally manipulative content is what loses monetisation, not AI itself.
